_meta.description: Forward-looking viewer-tier response for GET /api/vehicles. The viewer projection per rest-api.md §5.2.0 subtracts NOTHING from the owner field set and adds `sharePermission`. MYR-184 removed the previous `name` subtraction: the rider UI renders a shared car as '{Owner}'s {Vehicle}', and `name` is in the `required` list of vehicle-summary.schema.json, so masking it made every viewer row invalid against its own shape. Any field a future viewer mask removes MUST be optional in that schema. The viewer merge is LIVE as of MYR-184 (a rider who has redeemed an invite code sees these rows appended to their own cars), so this fixture is the canonical viewer response, not a forward-looking one. The MYR-233 `hasActiveRide` flag is in BOTH role allow-lists — it is derived operational state (P0, same tier as `status`), not owner-curated data. The MYR-286 `licensePlate` is in BOTH allow-lists too — a deliberate product decision, because the entire purpose of the plate is that a rider can identify the correct car at pickup. Contrast the full `vin`, which the catalog never carries at all (`vinLast4` only) and which the /snapshot gates to owners. The MYR-316 `serviceEstimatedEndAt` is in BOTH allow-lists too — P0 operational timing, same tier as `status`, and a rider needs it for exactly the reason the owner does: it FLOORS the scheduling picker. The first row is `parked`, so the value is `null` (no bound; scheduling stays fully open). The MYR-491 `setupState` is in BOTH allow-lists as well, and the SECOND row is why: a car whose owner has linked it but not yet paired the virtual key has never streamed, so `status` sits at the write-once `offline` schema default forever — and MYR-437 is the report that a rider's picker therefore calls a perfectly fine shared car 'offline', permanently, with no explanation and no way to book it. `setupState` is what lets the picker say 'still being set up' and grey the row with a reason instead. The viewer is the party the value is ABOUT, exactly as with `rideShareEnabled`. A `null` means NO CLAIM (the first row), never 'ready'. The MYR-507 `trimLabel` is in BOTH allow-lists as well, and the THIRD row is why — it is the field report verbatim. A rider was shown a shared car whose Live Activity subline read a bare 'UltraRed' and whose review-sheet row rendered the generic make 'Tesla', because the catalog carried a colour and nothing else identifying: the trim was withheld as detail-sheet-only, and a VIEWER NEVER FETCHES A SNAPSHOT, so there was no second surface to fall back to. `trimLabel` is an equipment fact of exactly the tier of its identity siblings `model`/`year`/`color` — all three already in both allow-lists, and all four legible through a windshield from the kerb — so there was never anything here for masking to protect. With the four together, that row renders the client's target descriptor exactly: '2026 Model X Plaid · Ultra Red'. Note `model` and `year` on that row are themselves MYR-507 values, VIN-derived: before it, a car the Go server provisioned carried '' and 0 permanently, which is the other half of why a rider had only a colour to go on. The MYR-515 `location` object is in BOTH allow-lists too, and this fixture is where that decision has to be justified: it is the FIRST P1 field on this resource other than `licensePlate`. The argument is that a viewer ALREADY receives latitude/longitude at full precision on the STREAMING path for exactly these vehicles — `vehicleStateViewerFields` retains the whole Speed/GPS atomic group, 'the entire point of a shared live map', and MYR-435's narrowing deliberately left it — so this is the same value over a different transport to a party already entitled to it. The honest caveat: the catalog hands a viewer N positions at once where the socket hands out one per subscription, which is an AGGREGATION difference rather than an entitlement one, since the grant is per-vehicle and a viewer could subscribe to each car in turn. Coarsening was considered and deliberately not applied — rounding this row while the socket serves the exact value protects nothing and degrades the short-hop pickup ETA the field exists for. Why the viewer needs it at all: the rider's picker ranks shared cars by pickup ETA, holds exactly ONE coordinate (the watched car's, off the single-vehicle socket subscription), and CANNOT fetch a per-row /snapshot — that is 403 by design (MYR-432/449). The second row shows the `null` state: a car that has never streamed has no fix. The MYR-581 `ownerFirstName` is in BOTH allow-lists, and THIS role is the one it exists for: a viewer had no way at all to learn the name of the person whose car they were granted, so the client fell back to the make and an incoming ride card read 'Tesla wants a ride' about a human being (MYR-532 item 4). It is P1 and it is a FIRST NAME ONLY, which is the whole reason it is safe here — the platform already hands this same viewer this same owner's first name in the redeem response and in the signed share link's `from`, so this row discloses nothing new, it just keeps it visible a week later. Rows one and three name their owners ('Alex', 'Amruth'); the second carries `null`, an owner who has never been asked for a name — and note that the SAME ladder gates offerability, so that car will refuse ride requests with `409 vehicle_unavailable` until its owner sets one (§7.26). `null` is NOT the empty string: drop the whole possessive fragment rather than rendering "'s Model Y".
